Set up Twilio

  1. Use your team's Twilio account and create a dedicated API key. Twilio API keys

  2. Choose a voice-capable incoming phone number owned by the account. MMHotline opens all connections to Twilio.

  3. Put the Twilio account SID, API key, and calling number in the settings file using the keys below, then apply the settings file. Before saving the setup, MMHotline checks with Twilio that the account owns the calling number and the number supports voice calls.

Settings file keys

  • Twilio account SID

    sending_services.twilio.account_sid

    The account that owns the calling number.

  • Twilio API key SID

    sending_services.twilio.api_key_sid

    Create a dedicated API key for MMHotline.

  • Twilio API key secret

    sending_services.twilio.api_key_secret

    The API key's secret.

  • Twilio calling number

    sending_services.twilio.phone_number_to_call_from

    An incoming phone number owned by the Twilio account and able to receive voice calls. Use a plus sign, country code, and number without spaces, such as +12025550102.

  • Extra phone numbers on the contact card (optional)

    sending_services.twilio.extra_phone_numbers_on_the_contact_card

    A list of phone numbers to include on the contact card, each with a plus sign, country code, and number without spaces, such as +12025550102. Use [] for none.

Example settings

sending_services:
  twilio:
    account_sid: <Twilio account SID>
    api_key_sid: <Twilio API key SID>
    api_key_secret: <Twilio API key secret>
    phone_number_to_call_from: <Twilio calling number>
    extra_phone_numbers_on_the_contact_card: []
Where Twilio is set up

Set in TEMPORARY-DIRECTORY/mmhotline_settings.yml, in sending_services.twilio. The file's first line says: Managed by MMX from mmhotline_settings.yml in the systems repository. Change it there and push; util01 applies it.

Times are New York time (America/New_York), the team's time zone.
